label: early original-phase j/v/k/h after a 0 or w (plus weak j at t=0)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at early positions t=0..4 (none at t>=6, never on the delimiter or in the copy phase). It fires almost only on the first occurrence of the input token. Input token is the main driver: j (17.6x lift, 42% of mass) and v (6.9x, 34%), then weaker k and h. Firing is strongly boosted when a 0 or w came earlier, especially right before (prev_tok 0: 7.6x, w: 4.2x). The strongest activations are things like w 0 [j] or z 0 0 [v] at t=2-3, and t=2-3 holds about 77% of the mass. j at t=0 fires often but weakly (31% of activations, about 4.5% of mass). Misses are a long tail of other tokens (k, f, n, 3) after a 0 at early positions. False positives are mostly v at t=0 and j/v at t=4 without a strong 0/w context. So it reads like an additive score (token identity + 0/w context + early position) rather than a clean boolean.
